theme: DAGMA against its authors' package on the NOTEARS and DAGMA papers' simulation, z-scored, rescaled, and raw
build: DAGMA: Andrey pre-release build of 10 November 2026 (the 0.17.0 release branch), the default fit of the 0.17.0 release; the rows are the 0.17.0 lane's shipped default
verdict_rule: DAGMA: per cell (noise, scale, graph, variables; 20 datasets): D = SHD(Andrey) - SHD(reference) per dataset, on the datasets both fitted; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)). The decision cells are the z-scored ones (claim in), 24: ER2 and SF4, 10 to 100 variables, three noises; the raw cells, where the least-squares fit reads the simulation's units, and the rescaled cells are reported, not judged (claim out), at 10 to 50 variables. No decision cell was worse than the reference, so none was rerun; the one rescaled cell worse on seeds 0-19 (SF4, 50 variables, Gaussian noise) was rerun on seeds 20-39 and is a tie there. The floor, per dataset: SHD(Andrey) minus SHD(empty graph); it applies where the reference's interval lies wholly below 0, and a row then passes when Andrey's does too. On the z-scored cells it applies in none: the reference is below the empty graph in none of the 24
fit_protocol: DAGMA: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, one timed fit without warm-up, a cap of 1,800 s per fit, past which a fit is a timeout and never scored; no fit failed or timed out. ratio is the median over the paired datasets of the reference's time over Andrey's, below 1 where Andrey is slower
error_metric: DAGMA: SHD of the DAG against the true DAG (a reversed edge counts 1), the papers' measure: andrey_shd, comparator_shd, and empty_shd are medians over the paired datasets, and the _mean fields their means. The _mec_ fields and mec are the SHD between the CPDAGs of the estimate and of the truth, reported and not judged
complete_definition: DAGMA: true when every row has at least 10 paired datasets (both fitted)
seeds_note: DAGMA: every cell holds 20 datasets, seeds 0-19; the one rescaled replication holds 20 fresh datasets, seeds 20-39

regimes.notears_paper_standardized: the NOTEARS and DAGMA papers' simulation: linear models with weights of magnitude 0.5 to 2 on Erdos-Renyi graphs with 2 d edges (ER2) or scale-free graphs with 4 d (SF4), Gaussian noise of unit variance, 1,000 rows, columns shuffled, every column z-scored
regimes.notears_paper_exponential_standardized: the NOTEARS and DAGMA papers' simulation: linear models with weights of magnitude 0.5 to 2 on Erdos-Renyi graphs with 2 d edges (ER2) or scale-free graphs with 4 d (SF4), Exponential noise of unit variance, 1,000 rows, columns shuffled, every column z-scored
regimes.notears_paper_gumbel_standardized: the NOTEARS and DAGMA papers' simulation: linear models with weights of magnitude 0.5 to 2 on Erdos-Renyi graphs with 2 d edges (ER2) or scale-free graphs with 4 d (SF4), Gumbel noise of unit variance, 1,000 rows, columns shuffled, every column z-scored
regimes.notears_paper_rescaled: the NOTEARS and DAGMA papers' simulation: linear models with weights of magnitude 0.5 to 2 on Erdos-Renyi graphs with 2 d edges (ER2) or scale-free graphs with 4 d (SF4), Gaussian noise of unit variance, 1,000 rows, columns shuffled, each variable divided by its standard deviation before its children read it
regimes.notears_paper_exponential_rescaled: the NOTEARS and DAGMA papers' simulation: linear models with weights of magnitude 0.5 to 2 on Erdos-Renyi graphs with 2 d edges (ER2) or scale-free graphs with 4 d (SF4), Exponential noise of unit variance, 1,000 rows, columns shuffled, each variable divided by its standard deviation before its children read it
regimes.notears_paper_gumbel_rescaled: the NOTEARS and DAGMA papers' simulation: linear models with weights of magnitude 0.5 to 2 on Erdos-Renyi graphs with 2 d edges (ER2) or scale-free graphs with 4 d (SF4), Gumbel noise of unit variance, 1,000 rows, columns shuffled, each variable divided by its standard deviation before its children read it
regimes.notears_paper: the NOTEARS and DAGMA papers' simulation: linear models with weights of magnitude 0.5 to 2 on Erdos-Renyi graphs with 2 d edges (ER2) or scale-free graphs with 4 d (SF4), Gaussian noise of unit variance, 1,000 rows, columns shuffled, the simulation's own units
regimes.notears_paper_exponential: the NOTEARS and DAGMA papers' simulation: linear models with weights of magnitude 0.5 to 2 on Erdos-Renyi graphs with 2 d edges (ER2) or scale-free graphs with 4 d (SF4), Exponential noise of unit variance, 1,000 rows, columns shuffled, the simulation's own units

hardware: DAGMA: AMD EPYC 7713 64-Core Processor, 1 core per fit, 1 BLAS thread; Andrey's fits and the recorded fits of the reference ran in separate runs on shared nodes of the same CPU model, so the time ratio is indicative and absolute times do not compare across rows

likelihood_path.about: robust=True of andrey.dagma and andrey.notears, the likelihood path of Deng et al. (2024) after the least-squares fit, before and after the term -log|det(I - W)| left its likelihood, beside the same path run with the authors' code and the empty graph, on the same datasets. One row per method, graph, size and scale; every value is a mean over the row's datasets
likelihood_path.data: the simulation of Deng et al. (2024), Appendix D.1, drawn with the simulator of the authors' package dagrad: linear Gaussian models, weights uniform on +-[0.5, 1.5], one noise standard deviation per variable uniform on [0.1, 0.7], 1,000 rows, Erdos-Renyi (er2) and scale-free (sf2) graphs with 2 d edges, columns shuffled; standardized z-scores each column of the drawn sample
likelihood_path.metric: SHD between the CPDAG of the estimate and the CPDAG of the true DAG, the measure of Deng et al. (2024)

arms.before: Andrey pre-release build of 14 November 2026, whose robust=True likelihood includes the term -log|det(I - W)|; the method at its defaults with robust=True
arms.now: Andrey pre-release build of 15 November 2026, whose continuous fits are those of the 0.18.0 release: the likelihood of robust=True without the term -log|det(I - W)|; the method at its defaults with robust=True
arms.reference: Algorithm 1 of Deng et al. (2024) as printed, around the unmodified single fits of the authors' package dagrad (commit 4ce4c5a): the warm start is dagrad's least-squares fit at its defaults, each step solves loss_fn='logll' with reg='mcp' from the last accepted weights at lambda 0.4 and delta 0.2, both times 0.8 after each accepted step, a step is accepted while the Gaussian negative log-likelihood strictly falls, and each fit is thresholded at 0.3, dagrad's default. For dagma rows the solver is method='dagma'; for notears rows method='notears' with optimizer='adam'. The paper gives no cap on the steps; the run allowed 50, which no fit reached. A cyclic output is repaired outside the authors' code by dropping the weakest edges until no cycle is left (reference_outputs_repaired counts the datasets)

likelihood_path.comparison: per dataset D = SHD(a) - SHD(b); bootstrap_95 is the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D over 10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0); better when it lies wholly below 0, worse when wholly above, a tie otherwise
likelihood_path.protocol: each fit in its own process with one BLAS thread, on nodes of AMD EPYC processors of the Zen 3 generation; a cap per fit of 2,400 s (the fits of the build after, and NOTEARS's of the build before) or 1,800 s (DAGMA's of the build before, and the reference's), which no fit reached; times are not published

sachs.about: andrey.dagma and andrey.notears, at their defaults and with robust=True, beside andrey.pc and andrey.ges at their defaults, on the Sachs data, raw and with every column z-scored. One row per method, sample and scale: all_rows is the error of the fit on every row, and resample_mean the mean error over 10 resamples of the rows
sachs.data: andrey.load_dataset('sachs'): 11 proteins and phospholipids; 853 observational measurements (conditions=False) and the 7,466 measurements of all nine experimental conditions (conditions=True), read as one sample
sachs.truth: the consensus network of the dataset, 17 edges
sachs.metric: SHD between the CPDAG of the estimate and the CPDAG of the consensus network; pc and ges return a CPDAG, which is compared as returned
sachs.resampling: rows drawn with replacement to the sample's size, default_rng(b) for b = 0 to 9; a standardized fit z-scores the resampled rows

varsortability.what: varsortability of the consensus network on the 853 observational measurements (Reisach et al., 2021)

sachs.build: Andrey pre-release build of 15 November 2026, whose continuous fits are those of the 0.18.0 release: the likelihood of robust=True without the term -log|det(I - W)|
sachs.protocol: each fit in its own process with one BLAS thread, on a node of AMD EPYC processors of the Zen 3 generation; a cap of 900 s per fit, which no fit reached; no fit failed; times are not published
